guide.title: Prague - Top 30 Cafes & Cocktail Bars
guide.description:
When I was living in Prague I started a quest to  fi nd the best cafes and cocktail
bars in Prague. This guide is the summary of places that I still really enjoy after
fi ve years living in Prague.
You will  fi nd:  21 cafes and co ff ee shops  10 special cocktail bars (the last one
will surprise you)  Places where you can get breakfast, cocktails and great food
throughout the day  A mix of cosy , laidback and upscale atmospheres for all
budgets
Delicious options for vegans and vegetarians
Detailed explanations for every single place
Unlike what I often hear, there can be great customer service in Prague. Come
with me on a journey where you feel welcome and attended by friendly sta ff .
Most of the listed places speak English so do not worry about learning Czech.
I hope you enjoy it!

If you’d like a more extensive or tailored recommendations, feel free to reach out:
IG @remgou

data.name: Cafe Letka
data.description: Tram Stop "Letenske Namesti" (Letna neighborhood) I could say that it is the best brunch place in Prague but I would be biased because I lived next door for 2,5 years. It is still my favorite brunch place in the city (when we could fi nd a free table!). The interior is quite unique and brings you back to the previous lives of the place: you can see an Art Nouveau mirror,  industrial lamps and chandeliers hanging together from the ceiling, and large wooden tables on the checkered fl oor. Instagram material for sure. You go there for breakfast, brunch, a light lunch or even a cocktail later in the day. Their brunch is to die for, with home-made bread and locally- sourced ingredients. They also serve a great co ff ee from the Five Elephant roastery, get their daily cakes from an espresso bar nearby and their beer from a Czech brewery. Located in the middle of Letna, it is a great place to start exploring the surroundings: you can visit the Technical Museum right in front of it or loose yourself in Letna park, just a few meters away. Attention please: they do not take reservations, make sure you come early in the morning to  fi nd a free table. Bistro 8 European Veverkova 8, 170 00 Praha 7-Letná, Czechia +420 730 511 973 Tram Stop "Strossmayerovo náměstí" (Holesovice neighborhood) Metro Stop "Jiriho Z Podebrad" (Vinohrady neighborhood) You go to Bistrot 8 for a healthy brunch or lunch, with vegan and gluten-free options,  in a cosy place. data.name: Pilot Cafe
data.description: Tram Stop "Letenske Namesti" (Letna Neighborhood) The atmosphere at Pilot is cosy with wooden tables, chairs and sofas. It is perfect to enjoy their delicious brunch and homemade deserts. According to my wife, this is the best English breakfast that she had in Prague. Their co ff ee is quite good as well, they select beans from small Czech and foreign roasters. Fun fact: the  fi rst time I visited Pilot, I thought it was written Pillow. I guess I did not pay attention to all the signs on the wall (the helix, the clocks with the names of cities around the world or the big frame with a painted plane). Attention please: they only take reservations by phone, one day in advance.

data.name: Můj šálek kávy
data.description: Tram stop "Krizikova" (Karlin neighborhood) It is thanks to cafés like "Muj Salek Kavy" (meaning "My Cup of Co ff ee") that Karlin is becoming an up-and-coming neighborhood in Prague. Once inside you instantly feel like at home, in a cosy living room. You see a very few wooden tables around, many bookshelves and even a  fi replace. Personally, the thing I remember the most from the interior is the bricks of the back wall covered in blue and yellow paint, with "Muj Salk Kavy" and a co ff ee mug painted in white. I remember sitting right next to it the  fi rst time I had brunch there. Co ff ee lovers cannot stop praising this café where you get a very good dripped,  fi ltered or pressed co ff ee from the Czech "Doubleshot" roastery. To go with your cup of co ff ee, they serve good breakfast and lunch with most ingredients being sourced from local farmers. And if that's not enough, they also have a proper brunch menu in the weekend. Personally, I love their English breakfast and creamy pancakes with cherry compote, chocolate crumble and farm curd. Good to know: they serve sourdough bread from their own bakery but you can also ask for gluten-free bread. Attention Please: due to the size of the place, getting a table without a reservation could almost be as a miracle. data.name: Café Savoy
data.description: Tram stop "Ujezd" (Mala Strana neighborhood) Completely di ff erent vibe at Café Savoy: you have a date with History in a gorgeous First-Republic café. This café has been around since 1893 and went through crazy times: it had to close during the 1st World War, was a recruiting o ffi ce for the communist police, before being a smoky haunt during the Velvet revolution (1989). Eating at Café Savoy means sitting under a Neo-Renaissance ceiling and beautiful chandeliers, next to large windows, in an Art Nouveau decor. It has a spacious interior and is also well-known for serving gargantuan breakfasts and a Viennese-style menu. Last but not least: its location between Kampa and Petrin Hill is ideal, making it a strategic café to rest and be wowed, before you continue your visit of Mala Strana. Attention please: the place is often crowded, it is recommended to book a table online before you go.

data.name: SmetanaQ Café & Bistro
data.description: Tram stop "Narodni Divadlo" (Old Town) Where art and co ff ee come together to look at the river together! SmetanaQ Café is the central piece of a building dedicated to art and design,  with regular exhibitions of contemporary art, a showroom and a designer shop. They serve breakfast every day until 1pm (2pm in the weekend). Special mention to the "SmetanaQ breakfast": a mix of avocado toast, egg Benedict and wa ffl e with mascarpone and strawberries. They also have an afternoon menu until 9pm. Good to know: They use free-range eggs  and most of the food they cook comes from Bohemia and Moravia, two Czech regions. I could not talk about SmetenaQ without mentioning their large windows that o ff er an amazing view on the Vltava river (that literally is on the other side of the train tracks) and the castle. Fun fact: SmetanaQ is part of the “Best of Prague 2023” list in the breakfast section. The Globe Bookstore And Café International Pštrossova 1925/6, Nové Město, 110 00 Praha-Praha 1, Czechia +420 224 934 203 Tram stop "Lazarska" (New Town) If you miss American cuisine and cannot wait to feel like at home with some comfort food: The Globe is for you. On top of being the largest English Bookstore in Prague, The Globe is a great café and restaurant that serves a full American brunch menu on the weekend. I still salivate from their "chicken & wa ffl es" and the "American pancake stack". data.name: Moment Bistro
data.description: Tram Stop "Vinohradská vodárna" (Vinohrady neighborhood) Finally a 100% vegan café in Prague (yes, you read this right). Their menu is terri fi c and would make any meat lover salivate. How do these sound? - scrambled tofu, herb butter, pickled vegetables, baked mushrooms, tempeh bacon, rawmasan - baked potato gnocci, creamy cauli fl ower sauce, asparagus, micro greens, peas, celeriac cracklings -- buckwheat pancakes with poppy seeds / syrup, stewed fruit and almond cream What I also like about this place is that they serve traditional Czech dishes such as the "svickova sauce with dumplings". The place is not big so I would recommend you to book a table beforehand. You can do so directly on their website. Martin's Bistro European Velehradská 1911/4, 130 00 Praha 3-Vinohrady, Czechia +420 774 100 378 Metro stop "Flora" (Vinohrady neighborhood) A sense of home in this family-owned restaurant. Welcome to an intimate and cosy cafe bathed in natural light in a small corner of Vinohrady. Only 10 tables and a wooden bar where you can sit. The menu is tiny and changes regularly. You can feel that the same way you are treated as a family member as soon as you enter, they pour the same kindness into their food. There are 5-6 dishes on the regular menu (and always vegetarian options) and a proper brunch menu served on Saturday. I did not get to try their mango quesadilla but it looks yummy. I did try their "Coq of Vin" that was exquisite. Last but not least, they o ff er a large selection of cocktails,

data.name: Café NONA
data.description: Tram stop "Národní divadlo" (New Town) A hidden café on the 2nd  fl oor of the the National Theatre, how cool is it? Just enter through the glass shell of the New Stage building and go up the staircase to the  fi rst  fl oor. I found it soothing to watch passer-byes in the busy Narodny street, while sitting by the window with a warm cup of co ff ee. They only serve a few homemade deserts but have premium Julius Meinl Co ff ee along with soft and alcoholic drinks. Fun fact: A few years ago they organized a few drum and bass concerts on Friday nights, transforming the café into a night club. I got to see Pola & Bryson live, it was quite an experience.

data.name: The Farm
data.description: Tram stop "Korunovační" (Holesovice neighborhood) "The Farm" is not a misleading name: what you eat is directly coming from local producers, straight to you plate. This urban café is laid back but modern with industrial touches: plain gray walls with hanging vintage bicycles, black industrial lamps, sofas and couches. They even have a small terrace where you can enjoy a nice meal or a co ff ee in the intimacy of their backyard. Whether you come for breakfast, lunch or dinner, there is always a curated list of delicious dishes to choose from: homemade cakes and pancakes, burgers, gluten-free wa ffl es, grilled halloumi cheese and a few salads. They also serve 6 di ff erent types of homemade limonades. My favorite dish? Their pancakes. I mean look at my face.  I could combine pancakes and wine in the evening, what a dream. From the quality of their ingredients to the experience eating there, you feel that you are taken care of. A few examples: - You can have all-day brunch (if this is not love, I don’t know what it is) - Complimentary water is served with lemon slices and fresh mint. - Their co ff ee comes from the Czech “Double shot” roastery, one of the best co ff ees in Prague - Their menu evolves according to the seasons, seasonal ingredients or new cooking techniques. Fun fact: The Farm is part of the “Best of Prague 2023” list in the cafe section. Café Pavlač European V. Nejedlého 487/23, 130 00 Praha 3-Žižkov, Czechia +420 702 124 556 Tram stop "Viktoria Žižkov" (Zizkov neighborhood)

data.name: Vnitroblock
data.description: Tram stop “Dělnická” (Holesovice neighborhood) At Vnitroblock you feel the soul of Holesovice, its past, its present and its future. Located in a former factory they turned the space into a hub of cultural and artistic experiences: - "Signature" is the cosy café right in the middle. You will also fi nd a gallery space for young designers and a  showroom for local and European brands. - "Pidikino" is their tiny cinema in the basement - "Sector" is the dance studio

data.name: Kavarna Pod Lipami
data.description: Tram stop "Korunovační" (Bubenec neighborhood) Cute name for a cute and cosy place: "Kavarna Pod Lipami" means the "Café Under the Lindens". The intro on their Facebook page says it all: "a neighborhood café with a range of quality products and friendly service". They serve a good premium co ff ee and you can choose from a few alternative brewing methods. You can also get a good breakfast or a light lunch. During the summer, you can sip a nice cup of co ff ee on their sunny terrace, while being just a few minutes away from Letna Park. Radost FX Fusion Bělehradská 234/120, 120 00 Vinohrady, Czechia +420 778 407 374 Tram & Metro Stop "I.P Pavlova" (Vinohrady neighborhood) Probably one of the best place for vegetarians in Prague. Before being a restaurant and a cafe, Radost is a night club (and it was one of the  fi rst to open before the Velvet Revolution). Personally I never partied there and only went to their café for a delicious and  fi lling Sunday brunch. I love two things there: - The comfy seats and sofas. Some are so  fl u ff y that you could fall asleep. - Their brunch menu has mostly American and Mexican dishes with a lot of choice, and everything is vegetarian. My all-time favorite was without a doubt one of their breakfast burritos. The regular menu is also quite large with a lot of fresh salads, a few vegan asian dishes, Italian cuisine and more. Fun fact: Rihanna recorded the movie clip of "Don't stop the music" in the Radost club. Marthy's Kitchen French Francouzská 13, 120 00 Praha 2-Vinohrady, Czechia

data.name: Antonínovo bakery
data.description: Metro stop "Namesti Miru" (Vinohrady neighborhood) Tram stop "Karlínské náměstí" (Karlin neighborhood) Tram stop Strossmayerovo náměstí (Holesovice neighborhood) Tram stop Arbesovo náměstí (Smichov neighborhood) I love Antonínovo bakery: the smell of freshly baked breads and pastries when you walk nearby and the bakers preparing the dough with passion in front of the customers. Beyond being a simple bakery, you can also sit there and enjoy a cup of well-roasted co ff ee, one of their daily soups or a light meal. If you are on a go and looking for a quick stop with tasty baked food, try Antonínovo.

data.name: Café Záhorský
data.description: Tram & Metro stop "Hradčanská" (Dejvice neighborhood) Cafe Zahorsky is your neighborhood family cafe in Dejvice, run by a couple who genuinely wants to  fi ll your day with kindness and fresh ingredients. Their breakfast menu is terri fi c: I always ordered eggs Benedict and there were always a delight. You can also choose from the "English Royal Breakfast", "the toast with avocado",  their "three eggs in a glass" or many other dishes. From breakfast to dinner, you can be sure that there will be great food for you to enjoy. The interior is very cosy with small wooden tables, hanging lamps from the ceiling and large windows. You will de fi nitely feel in a nice welcoming cocoon. Last but not least, they want this café to be a meeting point and regularly organize events like exhibitions, small concerts, wine tastings, parties... Make sure to check them out if you are around. Bars Parlour Cocktail Bar Czech Republic, Krakovská 15, 110 00 Nové Město, Czechia +420 777 200 015 Metro Stop "Muzeum" (New Town) Welcome to the most secret speakeasy in Prague. Without a doubt my favorite bar in the city ! Parlour is not just about cocktails, it is an entire experience: the entrance door is a bit hidden and it is very easy to walk past it. As soon as your enter and go down the stairs, you discover a small place with not more than 10 tables, some jazzy music and dim light. You would not believe that at the end of the street you get to the busy Wenceslas Square. No menu, the bartender comes to you and enquires about

data.name: Malkovich
data.description: Tram stop "Viktoria Zizkov" (Zizkov neighborhood) Enter Malkovich Bar and it feels like you get into someone's apartment from the 50s. The counter is quite small, you sit on old wooden chairs and sofas, surrounded by vintage wallpapers and candles. It is part of the experience! You de fi nitely go there for the quality of their signature cocktails, the special atmosphere of the place and to really feel Zizkov's vibe. Attention please: they do not serve food. Champagneria Wine Bar Průchodní 4, Staré Město, 110 00 Praha-Praha 1, Czechia +420 735 025 482 Metro Stop "Narodni Trida" (Old Town) Champagneria is the type of cute and hidden places that you would like to bump into more often. Not only a bar, it is also an art gallery and they organize live music performances. Drink-wise, Its name is quite self explanatory, they serve French champagnes and other sparking wines, at very reasonable prices. If you do not like bubbles, they also serve cocktails like the White Rabbit with Mezcal, or the Pac Man with Palenka. Fun Fact: you get the Pac Man for free if you beat the current high score in PAC-MAN They also serve a large diversity of warm and cold dishes, from snails to oysters going through sausages and grilled cheese.

data.name: Duplex
data.description: Metro Stop "Muzeum" or "Mustek" (New Town) Duplex is a night club but they also have a nice rooftop bar that overlooks Wenceslas Square. As soon as you get out of the elevator you will see colorful umbrellas on the ceiling. It is a nice  fi rst sight before you get to sit down and wait for your drink. If you are in the centre and want to enjoy some nice weather with a view and a drink, this is a great place to go. Bar and Books Cocktail Bar Mánesova 64, 120 00 Praha 2-Vinohrady, Czechia +420 222 724 581 Manesova Bar & Books: Tram stop "Vinohradská Tržnice" (Vinohrady Neighborhood) Tynska Bar & Books: Metro stop "Starometska" (New Town) Very intimate and chic atmosphere for this bar with speakeasy vibes. "The Most Refreshingly Civilized Places To Meet" to use their words. Great cocktail menu: my favorite is the rose gin & tonic but they also serve spicy mango margaritas, blueberry mule, popcorn old fashioned along with their own signature drinks. For connoisseurs, they o ff er an extensive selection of whisky and cigars. Good to know: they have live performances on Fridays and Saturdays along with burlesque shows.

data.name: Balcony Bar
data.description: Metro Stop "Mustek" (New Town) This rooftop bar has a great location, only a few minutes from the busy Wenceslas square. They serve a large diversity of gin & tonic (about 20 gins and 10 tonics), along with a long list of champagnes and wines. La Bodeguita del Medio Cuban Kaprova 19/5, 110 00 Staré Město, Czechia +420 724 461 678 Metro Stop "Starometska" (Old Town) If you feel in the mood of dancing to the rhythms of salsa and other latin dances, La Bodeguita del Medio is the place to be. This Cuban bar and restaurant has been around for more than 20 years and is well known among locals. You will  fi nd everything you need to have a great evening (and night):  homemade Cuban dishes, delicious Caribbean Cocktails and the aroma of Cuban cigars. The atmosphere of the old  colonial style will de fi nitely take you to La Havana for a few hours. Some of their classic cocktails include seven types of mojitos, a few caipirinhas, their Cuban classics and many more. Good luck to choose among all those nice sounding drinks. Cloud 9 Sky Bar at the Hilton Cocktail Bar Pobřežní 1, 186 00 Karlín, Czechia +420 224 842 999 Metro Stop "Florenc" (Karlin neighborhood) If you are looking for a chic, upscale, loungy bar with a view, the Sky Bar of the Hilton hotel is for you. You get quite a unique panorama with the Vltava River and the Prague skyline in front of you. In case of cold or rainy weather, you will not miss out on anything as there are glass walls all around.
